title: Vocabulary sets for body and treatment words plus a mimes guessing activity
summary: A matching exercise for pictures, a study tip on grouping vocabulary into sets (treatment, joints, verbs, body parts), and a pair activity where one student mimes a problem while the other guesses and gives advice.

title: Distinguishing hurt, sore, and pain in grammar and context
summary: A study tip explaining that hurt (verb), sore (adjective), and pain (noun) are not interchangeable, followed by a fill-in exercise requiring eight sentences to be completed with illness and injury vocabulary from a box.

title: Past continuous and past simple for actions interrupted mid-course
summary: Grammar explanations showing how past continuous and past simple work together to express an action happening during a longer one, with practice of a clinic dialogue about an injured wrist.
section: Lesson 2: I was ice skating, and I fell over

title: Practising past continuous and past simple with sentence completion
summary: Two exercises: one requires filling eight sentences with the correct past continuous or past simple forms, and the other asks students to complete six sentences with their own ideas in past simple.

title: Reading comprehension questions about Ammar's injury and recovery blog
summary: Six short-answer questions and five multiple-choice items based on a blog post describing how Ammar broke his back, his therapy progress, and his use of an exoskeleton.
section: Lesson 3: My friends were all watching, so I didn't want to give up

title: Retelling a story and practising -ing/-ed adjectives and -ful words
summary: Students retell Ammar's story sentence by sentence, then learn the difference between -ing and -ed adjectives and the spelling rule for -ful, with two fill-in exercises to reinforce both points.

title: Writing questions for smoking facts and using phrasal verb objects
summary: Students read texts with missing figures, listen to verify answers, write questions matching given responses about smoking statistics, and learn rules for object placement in phrasal verbs.
section: Lesson 4: Most smokers take it up as teenagers

title: Phrasal verb word order practice and negation prefixes for adjectives
summary: An exercise on placing verbs and objects correctly in sentences using phrasal verbs, plus an activity forming adjective opposites with the prefixes un-, in-, im-, and related rules.
